# HEVC fixtures

Real access units from the AMD iGPU's encoder, made with exactly the encoder lain-linux-video will use (spike 6's
`e2e.c`: libva, HEVC Main 4:2:0 8-bit, CBR with a two-frame HRD, one reference, lain's own VPS/SPS/PPS and slice
headers as packed headers) by `spikes/linux-convert/fixture/hevcfix`, fed synthetic NV12 (a moving gradient and a
square). Generated by the lead on 2026-10-31 under `nvidia-guard.sh`; each stream decodes with libde265 with no
errors or warnings (`spikes/linux-convert/e2e/decode-check.py`).

Each `au-NN.h265` is one encode result exactly as libva returned it (what `EncodedFrame.annexb` carries), in
encode order. Concatenated they are the stream.

| Directory | Size | Frames | Rate control | What it covers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `256x144/` | 256×144 | 8 | CBR 4 Mbps, bit stuffing off | IDR at 0, a requested IDR at 5 (parameter sets re-sent, byte-identical to the first) |
| `256x144-stuffing/` | 256×144 | 8 | CBR 4 Mbps, Mesa's default bit stuffing | the same, but `au-03` ends with a filler-data NAL unit (type 38, `FD_NUT`) |
| `192x128/` | 192×128 | 3 | CBR 3 Mbps, bit stuffing off | another size: different SPS bytes, so a new `VideoConfig` |

`manifest.txt` lists, per AU, what a plain start-code scan in the generator found (independent of the Rust code):

```
au-05.h265 size=7346 keyframe=1 nal=32,4,23,4 nal=33,31,44,4 nal=34,79,6,4 nal=19,89,7257,4
```

- `keyframe`: the AU holds an IRAP slice (NAL types 16–21).
- `nal=<type>,<offset>,<length>,<start code length>`: the NAL unit type; the offset of its 2-byte header in the file;
  its length from that header on, without trailing zero bytes; and the start code before it (3, or 4 with the
  leading zero byte).

Observed in these streams: every start code is 4 bytes; a keyframe AU is VPS, SPS, PPS, then one `IDR_W_RADL` slice;
other AUs are one `TRAIL_R` slice; there is no access unit delimiter or SEI. With bit stuffing on (Mesa's default for
CBR) the encoder pads frames below the rate's per-frame budget with filler data. At a budget larger than the coded
buffer that overflows it, and libva returns only the wrapped tail. lain-linux-video should set
`rc_flags.disable_bit_stuffing`, and the core drops filler NAL units anyway.
